title: Zesty Velvety Tunisian Lamb Tagine
description: A flavorful, one-pot Tunisian dish featuring lamb, peppers, and a hint of sweetness from the raspberries. This velvety tagine is perfect for a weeknight dinner or a special occasion.
instructions: Heat oil in a large clay or ceramic tagine or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown the lamb pieces in batches until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes. Transfer the lamb to a plate and set aside.
Add the sliced red bell pepper and yellow onion to the pot and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the browned lamb, chicken broth, and raspberries to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then cover the pot and transfer it to the oven.
Bake at 300°F (150°C) for 2 1/2 hours, or until the lamb is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Remove the pot from the oven and let it cool slightly.
Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan, discarding the solids.
Return the lamb to the saucepan and simmer over medium heat until the sauce has thickened to your liking.
Season the tagine with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve the tagine hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
Let the tagine cool to room temperature, then refrigerate or freeze it for up to 3 days or up to 2 months, respectively.
To serve, let the tagine come to room temperature. If frozen, thaw it overnight in the refrigerator. Then, reheat the tagine over low heat, stirring occasionally, until warmed through.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
